answerNotes.BOWL: A bowl has raised curved sides. That shape helps hold liquid or contain a mixture while it is stirred.
answerNotes.BUTTER: Butter is made by churning cream. It adds flavor and fat to baked goods as well as serving as a spread.
answerNotes.SALT: Salt is a seasoning usually paired with pepper on the table. A pinch describes a small amount rather than a special kind of it.
answerNotes.HOT: Hot describes temperature. A hot dog is a food name, so the two-word phrase has a meaning beyond the adjective alone.
answerNotes.LID: A lid is a removable cover. On a cooking pot it helps contain heat and steam; on a jar it closes the opening.
answerNotes.PAN: Pan is a broad kitchen word. A frying pan is used on a stove, while a loaf pan holds dough or batter in the oven.
answerNotes.WHITE: White is a color description, not a flower or bird name. Crossings can help when a clue asks for a color rather than a species.
answerNotes.SHARE: Share means give part of something to others. In a meal setting it can concern food rather than dividing property or money.

answerNotes.SLICE: A slice is a flat cut portion of food. Slice can also be the action of cutting food into those portions.
answerNotes.PEEL: Peel can name an outer covering or the action of removing it. Citrus rind and potato skin are familiar examples.
answerNotes.GREEN: Green describes many growing leaves. It is also a color name in its own right, so read whether the clue asks for a plant or its appearance.
answerNotes.BOWL: A bowl has raised curved sides. That shape helps hold liquid or contain a mixture while it is stirred.

answerNotes.CINNAMON: Cinnamon comes from bark. It is sold in rolled sticks as well as ground into a fine powder.
answerNotes.BREAD: Bread may be a whole loaf or pieces cut from it. A loaf is counted as a whole, while a slice is one flat portion.
answerNotes.BUTTER: Butter is made by churning cream. It adds flavor and fat to baked goods as well as serving as a spread.
answerNotes.SUGAR: Sugar sweetens baking mixtures and drinks. Granulated sugar and powdered sugar have different textures despite sharing the same sweet ingredient.
answerNotes.SLICE: A slice is a flat cut portion of food. Slice can also be the action of cutting food into those portions.
answerNotes.CRUST: Crust can mean a pie's pastry shell or a loaf's baked outer surface. Both are outer parts, but they are made differently.
answerNotes.WARM: Warm is a relative temperature word. Something warm has more heat than a cool object but is not usually described as hot.
answerNotes.PLATE: A plate is flatter than a bowl. Its broad surface is useful for separate portions of a meal.
answerNotes.KNIFE: A knife cuts with a blade. In the kitchen, the board beneath the food supports the ingredient while it is sliced.
